headline: APOLLO SILVER'S EJIDO VOTES TODAY ON LIFTING 13-YEAR BAN — CINCO DE MAYO COULD FINALLY OPEN FOR DRILLING
snippet: Ejido Benito Juárez in Buenaventura Municipality, Chihuahua, Mexico is holding a community assembly today, September 20, 2026, to vote on lifting the mining moratorium imposed in 2012 that has kept Apollo Silver Corp. from conducting systematic exploration at its optioned Cinco de Mayo silver project — the first time in over a decade that community members will get to vote on rescinding the ban; Apollo announced the vote on September 10 and reaffirmed its commitments on September 14, pledging independent aquifer and water-supply studies as its central concession to address the community's core concern that new mining activity could worsen water stress in an already dry region; a vote in favour lifts the moratorium and allows Apollo to begin early-stage field programs immediately, opening one of the most significant locked-away silver exploration targets in the Americas; a no vote leaves the Cinco de Mayo project effectively frozen and would require Apollo to seek a future vote or renegotiate its community relationship from scratch; the Cinco de Mayo property in Chihuahua is considered high-potential based on historical surface sampling but has never received modern systematic drilling because of the ejido's ban; the outcome is expected to be announced following today's assembly.

headline: GENERATION MINING FULLY FUNDS C$1.3B MARATHON MINE — ONTARIO COPPER-PALLADIUM PROJECT STARTS CONSTRUCTION Q4 2026
source_name: Generation Mining / Canada Growth Fund / Newswire.ca
snippet: Generation Mining has secured the final C$340 million tranche to complete a C$1.3 billion capital package for its Marathon copper-palladium project in Northwestern Ontario, clearing the path for construction to begin in Q4 2026; the Canada Growth Fund committed approximately C$140 million structured as roughly C$90 million in common equity and a C$50 million convertible note, while the Ontario government added $11 million from its Critical Minerals Processing Fund; the fully financed capital structure eliminates the project's last major development risk and allows the company to advance toward a mine that will produce an average of 42 million pounds of copper, 168,000 ounces of palladium, and 38,000 ounces of platinum annually once operating; Marathon is notable as one of the very few primary palladium deposits in the Western world at a time when palladium supply remains heavily concentrated in Russia's Norilsk operations, giving the project strategic significance beyond its copper economics; the successful capital raise at C$1.3 billion despite a hawkish rate environment demonstrates that critical-minerals projects with palladium-copper exposure can still attract institutional and government capital in 2026 — a benchmark for other development-stage critical minerals juniors seeking project financing.

headline: US AND DENMARK SIGN HISTORIC GREENLAND SECURITY PACT — BANS ADVERSARY INVESTMENT IN CRITICAL MINERALS, CEMENTS RARE EARTH SUPPLY LINE
snippet: The United States and Denmark signed a historic trilateral security agreement covering Greenland, announced September 18, 2026, that provides for a substantially expanded and enduring U.S. military presence on the island while explicitly banning adversary nations from establishing military positions or making sensitive investments in Greenland including its critical mineral deposits; the agreement limits the ability of non-NATO nations to invest in sensitive areas such as rare earth, copper, and precious metals mining assets, directly addressing a strategic risk that had previously made international capital cautious about committing to Greenland exploration projects; Greenland Mines (NASDAQ: GRML) — which holds the Sarfartoq neodymium-praseodymium project (up to $2.05 billion estimated NPV, targeting production capacity equal to 34% of all NdPr oxide refined outside China annually) and the Skaergaard palladium-platinum-gold system — issued a statement applauding the agreement as reinforcing the geopolitical legitimacy of Western-aligned Greenland mining investment; the accord arrives 53 days before the November 10, 2026 expiry of China's suspension of rare earth export controls, a structural backdrop that makes every additional Western NdPr tonne in development increasingly strategic; for junior mining investors, the agreement signals that Greenland is now a politically stable, Western-supported exploration jurisdiction in a way that had not been credibly established before.

headline: AMERICAS GOLD HITS BEST GRADES EVER AT COSALA — 654 g/t Ag, 1.5% Cu OVER 20.5 METRES IN MEXICO SILVER-COPPER COMPLEX
snippet: Americas Gold and Silver Corporation (TSX: USA) announced September 17 the best grade-width combination drilled to date at its Cosalá Complex in Sinaloa, Mexico: a lead intercept of 654.7 g/t Ag and 1.5% Cu over 20.5 metres from the San Rafael Upper deposit and a second intercept of 409.3 g/t Ag and 0.8% Cu over 14.1 metres from the 120 Upper deposit — both from infill and step-out holes drilled in the first half of 2026 at three deposit zones (San Rafael Upper, 120 Upper, 120 Lower); management notes that multiple holes across all three zones are returning substantially higher silver grades than the currently modeled resource, indicating the mineral resource estimate understates the deposit's actual grade and setting up a material upward revision in the next update; this is a separate release from the company's simultaneous Galena Complex program in Idaho's Coeur d'Alene silver district (which generated headlines this week for a 1,062 g/t Ag new vein discovery), reinforcing Americas Gold and Silver's position as one of the most active primary silver exploration programs in the Americas by metres drilled in 2026; the Cosalá Complex was acquired by Americas Gold and Silver in 2021 and the ongoing resource conversion program is the company's largest since acquisition.

headline: MARONAN METALS CONFIRMS WIDE HIGH-GRADE SILVER-LEAD ZONES IN QUEENSLAND — 11m AT 10.3% Pb AND 116 g/t Ag WITH RESOURCE UPDATE AHEAD
snippet: Maronan Metals (ASX: MMA) reported September 18 assay results from 13 drill holes in its ongoing 40,000-metre infill program at the Maronan Underground Project in northwest Queensland, confirming strong silver-lead mineralisation across both the Western and Eastern Horizons: best result MRN26013 (Western Horizon) returned 11.0 metres at 10.3% lead and 116 g/t silver, including a high-grade subinterval of 4.1 metres at 17.0% lead and 220 g/t silver; MRN26013 Eastern Horizon returned a standout silver grade of 2.0 metres at 4.2% lead and 533 g/t silver from 491.4 metres depth, among the highest-grade silver intercepts in the program to date; approximately 15,000 metres of the 40,000-metre program have been completed, with the data feeding a resource update planned for Q4 FY2027 ahead of a pre-feasibility study; the Maronan project sits in northwest Queensland's same base-metals belt that hosts the historic Century zinc mine and several major Cu-Pb-Zn systems, giving the project strong geological and infrastructure context; for ASX investors tracking the silver supply deficit story — six consecutive annual deficits confirmed through 2026, with this year's shortfall forecast at 46.3 million ounces — MMA represents a catalyst-rich primary silver development story with consistent infill drilling confirming resource growth potential.

headline: EU CLEARS ANGLO-TECK COPPER MEGADEAL — CHINA AND SOUTH KOREA ARE THE ONLY REMAINING OBSTACLES TO A TOP-5 GLOBAL PRODUCER
snippet: The European Union has cleared the merger between Anglo American and Teck Resources after regulators signalled the absence of competition concerns, leaving China and South Korea as the only outstanding jurisdictions in a deal designed to create Anglo Teck plc, a top-five global copper producer; Anglo American targets merger completion between September 2026 and March 2027 and identified Chinese anti-trust approval as the final major regulatory milestone remaining as of July 2026; the transaction combines Anglo American's copper operations — including the Quellaveco mine in Peru and existing Chilean assets — with Teck's QB2 copper mine in Chile and its steelmaking coal business, creating a combined copper production base that would rank alongside BHP and Rio Tinto in scale; both companies' shareholders approved the merger in December 2025, and the Investment Canada Act clearance was received the same month; for junior copper developers, the formation of a new mega-producer historically compresses the acquisition discount applied to development-stage copper assets as the surviving majors seek to replace the internal resource base they have consumed through corporate reorganisation, creating a more competitive M&A environment for permitted copper projects in the two to three years following such mergers.

headline: ICONIC MINERALS HITS 180-FOOT NEAR-SURFACE GOLD-SILVER CORRIDOR AT NEW PASS, NEVADA — BULK TONNAGE OXIDE SYSTEM EXPANDS
snippet: Iconic Minerals (TSXV: ICM) announced September 17 the second batch of assay results from its 2026 drilling program at the New Pass gold property in Churchill County, Nevada: five of six holes returned continuous near-surface gold-silver mineralisation from 30 to 180 feet (9–55 metres) at grades typical of bulk-tonnage heap-leach style systems — highlight intercepts include 180 feet (55 metres) grading 0.44 g/t Au and 3.21 g/t Ag in hole NP2613 and 160 feet at 0.37 g/t Au and 5.49 g/t Ag in hole NP2614; the results extend the mineralised footprint established in the first batch and confirm the oxide gold-silver system continues laterally beyond the historic resource outline; the final batch of samples has been submitted to ALS for analysis, representing the complete assay database for the 2026 program; New Pass sits in Churchill County, Nevada, within a geological corridor that hosts several past-producing heap-leach gold districts and within trucking distance of established processing infrastructure — the combination of near-surface position, consistent widths, and oxide metallurgy positions it for the type of low-capital-cost development path that has attracted major producer interest in comparable Nevada bulk-tonnage discoveries.

headline: FAST-TRACKING EVERY MINE IN DEVELOPMENT TODAY STILL CAN'T CLOSE THE GOLD-SILVER-COPPER DEFICIT BY 2030 — THE STRUCTURAL CASE
snippet: Discovery Alert's 2026 mining supply analysis quantifies a structural reality that underpins the junior mining investment case: even if every copper, silver, and gold project currently in development were fast-tracked from today, the combined structural supply deficit in all three metals would persist well into the early 2030s due to permitting lead times, capital allocation constraints, and the long construction-to-production timelines inherent to modern mine development; for copper, forecast demand growth from data centres, EV production, and grid buildout implies a deficit of 4-6 million tonnes per year by 2030 that no credible pipeline of currently funded projects can close; silver's sixth consecutive annual deficit at 46.3 million ounces in 2026 compounds against a cumulative 762-million-ounce drawdown of above-ground stocks since 2021 — stocks that cannot be quickly replenished because most silver is produced as a by-product of other metals rather than from dedicated silver mines where higher prices immediately incentivise production; gold mine output has been essentially flat since 2018 at approximately 3,600-3,700 tonnes per year despite record prices exceeding $4,000 per ounce, confirming that the price signal alone does not quickly unlock new supply when project pipelines are constrained by geology and regulation; the analysis directly reinforces the core junior mining investment thesis: structural commodity supply scarcity justifies development-stage risk premiums for quality projects even at current elevated metal prices.

headline: CAMECO CUTS McARTHUR RIVER GUIDANCE AND KAZATOMPROM LOWERS OUTPUT — URANIUM SPOT REBOUNDS TO $82 AS NORTHSHORE INDEX SOARS 17%
snippet: Uranium spot prices recovered sharply in September 2026 to approximately $82 per pound (up 8.05% on the month) as supply-side risks emerged simultaneously from two of the world's largest uranium producers: Cameco cut its McArthur River production guidance while Kazatomprom lowered its 2026 output projections, both reinforcing a structural deficit narrative that had appeared to soften when spot prices peaked near $95 per pound in August; the Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index advanced 17.01% for September while junior uranium miners tracked by broader indices gained approximately 21.75%, indicating that equity markets are treating the supply cuts as structurally meaningful rather than operational noise; long-term contract prices near $96.50 per pound continue to sit above spot — a forward premium structure signalling that utilities are willing to pay above current spot for guaranteed long-term supply security; the September spot price floor above $80 per pound, combined with Cameco's guidance reduction at its flagship asset, removes two of the primary bearish scenarios from the near-term risk matrix for uranium junior developers: price collapse and credible supply adequacy from existing producers; for junior uranium explorers particularly on the TSX-V and ASX, the guidance cuts are the clearest catalyst signal since 2024's spot peak that institutional capital is once again needed to fund new uranium supply.

headline: WHICH ASX GOLD MINERS CAN ACTUALLY WIN WITH A HAWKISH FED? THE AISC AND ROYALTY SCREEN THAT SEPARATES WINNERS FROM TRAPS
snippet: Discovery Alert's September 2026 analysis of Australian-listed gold producers identifies the structural characteristics that separate miners genuinely insulated from hawkish monetary policy from those that look resilient on surface metrics but face hidden margin compression: key filters include whether the producer's AUD-denominated cost base provides a natural hedge against USD gold price volatility (AUD typically weakens on rate-hike sentiment, compressing USD-equivalent operating costs while gold revenues remain in USD), whether the asset sits in a sliding-scale royalty bracket that accelerates above current gold price levels, and whether the operation relies on grid electricity versus diesel for energy; the analysis highlights that Australia's gold sector presents a uniquely favourable structural position in a hawkish-rate environment because the AUD-USD relationship acts as an automatic stabiliser for Australian producers when US rates rise — AUD weakness on rate hikes effectively reduces the USD cost of Australian mine operations at exactly the moment when gold prices in AUD may soften; the piece identifies the characteristics clustering in the mid-tier ASX producers but occasionally appearing in high-quality ASX juniors transitioning to production: sub-A$2,000 per ounce all-in sustaining costs, low royalty exposure at current gold prices, and balance sheets capable of organic growth without dilutive equity raises — the combination that allows a producer to continue growing cash flow even when the gold price in AUD is flat.
